notes:
Background: Lodestar builds personalization and bid-routing models for large DSP customers. Approached Redwood in Q3 2024 to replace an aging GPU fleet.

Sales/Procurement summary:
- Initial intro 2024-09-10 (Maya/Diego) - strong interest in deterministic latency for personalization (p99 < 30ms for 512-token hot paths).
- Completed technical deep-dive 2024-10-22 (SE-led). POC approved: 2-week Dedicated proof-of-concept (GPU pool + VPC peering).
- POC results (Dec 2024): Redwood runtime showed 18-28% lower per-token cost for bursty inference and stable p99 under load. Diego ran traceroutes + perf logs attached in Drive.
- Security review started 2024-12-05; security requested evidence of SOC2-like controls, KMS integration, and export logs to Splunk. We provided design + audit log examples.
- Procurement came back Jan 2025 with counteroffer from incumbent cloud provider (AWS) offering credits and a managed-endpoints migration path (SageMaker endpoints + VPC endpoints).

Why lost / current status:
- Decision: procurement selected "hyperscaler managed endpoints" (AWS) due to existing enterprise discount, single-vendor policy, and immediate credits that offset near-term runway risk.
- Internal blockers: Head of Infrastructure enforced vendor consolidation; CTO departure removed internal champion; finance placed hiring freeze and pushed cost normalization.
- Security team favorite: native IAM integration, centralized CloudTrail + CloudWatch pipelines, and vendor SLA alignment. These were perceived as lower integration risk than a new vendor.
- We pushed Dedicated + VPC (can support KMS/HSM + audit logging); technical fit accepted but business decision overrider.

Callouts / sales learnings:
- Hyperscalers frequently win on procurement credits + operational consolidation even when niche vendor shows cost/perf benefits.
- Need stronger procurement collateral: TCO model that includes migration & operational costs vs credits, and a template for STS/KMS + SIEM integration to shorten security approval.
- Missing champion risk: identify and cultivate at least two exec sponsors (infra + product) in enterprise deals.

Stated next steps from Lodestar: close vendor selection with AWS (internal comms 2025-02-05). They invited Redwood to re-engage in 6-9 months if consolidation review resumes or if latency/cost issues appear in managed endpoints.

Internal Redwood action items:
- Diego: capture final POC telemetry and produce a one-pager comparing run-costs vs AWS with the team's comments (owner: Diego, due 2025-02-20).
- Maya: send closure note + thank-you + ask for a short 15-min feedback call with Security (owner: Maya, due 2025-02-18).
- Product: draft quick-start for SIEM/KMS integration to reduce security friction (owner: product infra).

Quote snippets from Lodestar execs:
- "Great tech, but we can't justify a new vendor given the credits and our vendor consolidation policy."
- "If performance degrades on the managed endpoints, we'll reach back out."
timeline: 2025-02-05 - Exec decision to go with AWS managed endpoints; Redwood notified
